question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹1,200 at an interest rate of 3% per month in 6 months.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective simple interest rate for 6 months = 3% × 6 = 18%.

Simple Interest = 18% of ₹1200.

⇒ SI = (18 ÷ 100) × 1200 = 216

**∴ The correct answer is ₹216.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹1200

Rate of Interest (R) = 3% per month

Time (T) = 6 months

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

*(Note: Since the rate is given per month and time is in months, both units are matching and no conversion to years is needed.)*

 
 ₹1200

 Total Interest = 18% of ₹1200

**Calculation:**

⇒ SI = (1200 × 3 × 6) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 12 × 18

⇒ SI = 216

**∴ The correct answer is ₹216.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Consistency in Simple Interest

Always ensure that the Time (T) unit strictly matches the Rate (R) period. If Rate is monthly, Time must be in months. If Rate is per annum, Time must be in years.

Total Amount Formula

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI). This indicates the total sum that must be repaid after the time duration.

Simple vs Compound Interest

Simple Interest is charged only on the original principal sum for the entire tenure, whereas Compound Interest adds previously earned interest to the principal before calculating the next period's interest.
